description: Graduate course on building software whose failure can hurt people: hazard analysis, fault trees and FMEA, safety cases, fault tolerance, safety-critical coding, reliability modelling and the overlap with security. Students analyse real accident patterns in scenarios, model failures mathematically, build redundancy on the hardware bench and assemble a safety case for a medical or transport system.
modelledOn: Leveson, Engineering a Safer World: Systems Thinking Applied to Safety
Knight, Fundamentals of Dependable Computing for Software Engineers
IEC 61508 functional safety standard and the Goal Structuring Notation community standard
outcomes: Identify hazards and assess risk for a software-intensive system using HAZOP and STPA.
Build and analyse fault trees and FMEA tables, computing minimal cut sets and failure probabilities.
Construct a safety case with explicit claims, arguments and evidence and assess its confidence.
Design fault-tolerant architectures with redundancy, diversity and error recovery, and quantify their benefit.
Apply safety-critical coding rules and verification techniques, and model reliability with block diagrams, Markov models and growth models.
Analyse the interaction of safety and security threats and recommend integrated mitigations.

units.title: Dependability concepts and accidents
topics: Dependability attributes: reliability, availability, safety, integrity and maintainability
Faults, errors and failures: the chain of threats and fault classification
Accident case studies: Therac-25, Ariane 5 and the Boeing 737 MAX flight control software
Safety versus reliability versus security: why a reliable system can still be unsafe
Safety lifecycle and standards: IEC 61508, ISO 26262, DO-178C and IEC 62304

units.title: Hazard analysis and risk assessment
topics: Hazard identification: preliminary hazard analysis and HAZOP guide words
STPA: control structures, unsafe control actions and loss scenarios
Risk assessment: severity, likelihood, risk matrices and the ALARP principle
Safety integrity levels: SIL, ASIL and DAL and how they are assigned
Deriving safety requirements and tracing them to design and tests
Human factors in hazard analysis: operator error, mode confusion and alarm floods

units.title: Fault trees, FMEA and event trees
topics: Fault tree construction: gates, basic events and minimal cut sets
Quantitative fault tree analysis: top-event probability and importance measures
FMEA and FMECA: failure modes, effects, detection and risk priority numbers
Event trees and bow-tie diagrams linking causes to consequences
Software in fault trees and FMEA: modelling software failure modes and their limits
Common-cause failures and the beta-factor model

units.title: Safety cases and assurance arguments
topics: Assurance case structure: claims, arguments and evidence
Goal Structuring Notation: goals, strategies, solutions, contexts and assumptions
Confidence in arguments: defeaters, assurance deficits and eliminative argumentation
Certification and regulatory submissions for medical and transport software
Maintaining a safety case through change and operational feedback

units.title: Fault tolerance and redundancy
topics: Redundancy: hardware, information, time and software; triple modular redundancy and voting
Software diversity: N-version programming and recovery blocks, and their limits
Error detection: watchdog timers, assertions, checksums and error-correcting codes
Recovery and degraded modes: checkpointing, rollback, fail-safe, fail-operational and graceful degradation
Byzantine faults and agreement among redundant channels

units.title: Coding standards and verification for safety-critical software
topics: Coding standards: MISRA C, CERT C and language subsets such as SPARK
Defensive programming, assertions and design by contract
Static analysis and abstract interpretation for run-time error freedom
Testing criteria: statement, branch and MC/DC coverage and requirements-based testing
Formal methods in safety: model checking and proof of safety properties
Tool qualification, deterministic timing and worst-case execution time analysis

units.title: Reliability modelling
topics: Reliability function, hazard rate, the bathtub curve; exponential and Weibull models
MTTF, MTBF, MTTR and availability calculations
Reliability block diagrams: series, parallel and k-out-of-n systems
Markov models of repairable systems and steady-state availability
Software reliability growth models: Jelinski-Moranda and Goel-Okumoto
Statistical testing, operational profiles and the evidence needed for failure-free demonstration

units.title: Safety, security and organisational practice
topics: Security attacks with safety consequences: industrial control systems, medical devices and vehicles
Co-engineering safety and security: STPA-Sec and threat modelling against safety goals
Incident investigation: root cause analysis, just culture and safety culture
Safety management systems and organisational factors
Ethics, liability and regulation, with examples relevant to Ghana such as health devices and power infrastructure
Capstone: safety case for an infusion pump or a vehicle braking function

schedule.title: Dependability and learning from accidents
schedule.exercise: Write the fault-error-failure chain for the Ariane 5 and Therac-25 accidents, and explain with an example why a perfectly reliable component can be unsafe.

tasks.title: Classify the faults, errors and failures in a short accident account, then compare your chain with the expected answer
Investigate a Therac-style overdose case in the scenario engine, find the contributing software and process causes and score your findings against the rubric
Argue for or against a design in which a perfectly reliable controller meets its specification yet causes a hazard, scored on the safety versus reliability rubric

schedule.title: HAZOP, STPA and risk matrices
schedule.exercise: Run a HAZOP on an infusion pump dose calculation, sketch the STPA control structure, and place the identified hazards on a risk matrix with ALARP decisions.

tasks.title: Rate severity and likelihood for eight hazards of an infusion pump, place them on the risk matrix and mark which need mitigation to reach ALARP
Draw a control loop for a pump with HAZOP guide words applied to each signal and list the deviations and their consequences
Draw the STPA control structure of a minibus braking system, list unsafe control actions in four categories and write the loss scenarios

schedule.title: Integrity levels, requirements and human factors
schedule.exercise: Assign integrity levels to four functions of a train crossing controller, derive three safety requirements with trace links, and critique an alarm panel for operator overload.

tasks.title: Determine the safety integrity level of four functions from severity, exposure and controllability and check against the reference table
Trace a hazard through a safety requirement, a design element and a test case on a traceability diagram and find a missing link
Analyse an alarm flood incident in a power control room case, identifying mode confusion and proposing display and alarm changes scored by rubric

schedule.title: Fault tree analysis
schedule.exercise: Build a fault tree for loss of braking in a vehicle, find the minimal cut sets, compute the top-event probability and rank the importance of basic events.

tasks.title: Draw a fault tree for no output from a two-sensor alarm, using AND and OR gates, and list its minimal cut sets
Compute the top-event probability of a fault tree from basic-event probabilities and rank the events by Fussell-Vesely importance
Write a program that extracts minimal cut sets from a fault tree description and computes top-event probability, testing against a hand-solved tree

schedule.title: FMEA, event trees and common cause
schedule.exercise: Complete an FMEA table for a pump controller, draw a bow-tie for overdose and show how a common cause failure defeats a redundant pair.

tasks.title: Fill in an FMEA table for a pump, scoring severity, occurrence and detection, and sort the failure modes by risk priority number
Draw a bow-tie diagram for a medication overdose with causes, preventive barriers, recovery barriers and consequences
Model a redundant pair with a beta-factor common cause term, and plot system failure probability against beta from 0 to 0.2

schedule.title: Safety case construction
schedule.exercise: Write a GSN safety case for the claim that an infusion pump software is acceptably safe, listing evidence for each goal and the weakest link in your argument.

tasks.title: Draw the top three levels of a Goal Structuring Notation diagram for an infusion pump with goals, a strategy and contexts
Review a given safety case for missing evidence, invalid inferences and unsupported claims, and list the changes needed
Identify defeaters in a safety argument and rate assurance deficits, deciding what extra evidence would raise confidence enough to certify

schedule.title: Redundancy, voting and detection
schedule.exercise: Compute the reliability of a TMR system against a single module, design a voter, and explain why N-version software is not as independent as hoped.

tasks.title: Step a triple modular redundancy voter with one faulty channel injected and show the output stays correct for each fault position
Add a watchdog timer to a microcontroller control loop, inject a hang, and measure the time until the safe reset is triggered
Run three independently written versions of a function against 10,000 random inputs, measure coincident failures and compare with the independence assumption

schedule.title: Recovery, degraded modes and agreement
schedule.exercise: Design a fail-safe and a fail-operational mode for a train door controller and show how three channels agree when one sends conflicting values.

tasks.title: Build a sensor input with a redundant pair, detect disagreement, and force the output to a safe state with a status LED
Step a checkpoint and rollback recovery of a small computation through two injected errors and compare final state with the fault-free run
Step an agreement protocol among four channels with one Byzantine sender, and show how many faulty channels the vote tolerates

schedule.title: Safe coding, coverage and timing
schedule.exercise: Rewrite a C function so it follows six coding rules, identify run-time error sources with static analysis reasoning, and design tests to reach MC/DC.

tasks.title: Fix ten violations of MISRA-style rules (unbounded loops, unchecked returns, implicit conversions) in a C function and rerun its tests
Design the smallest test set achieving MC/DC for a decision with four conditions and verify coverage with an instrumented run
Use interval analysis on a small function to prove absence of overflow and array index errors, and find an input that breaks the unproved case

schedule.title: Reliability functions and block diagrams
schedule.exercise: Compute reliability and availability for a clinic server with repair, draw the reliability block diagram of a duplicated power supply and evaluate k-out-of-n options.

tasks.title: Plot exponential and Weibull reliability curves for the same MTTF and read the probability of survival at 1,000 hours
Compute the reliability of a series-parallel block diagram and compare it with a 2-out-of-3 arrangement across mission times
Compute steady-state availability for a rural clinic power system from failure and repair times and decide whether a second generator pays off

schedule.title: Markov models and software reliability growth
schedule.exercise: Solve a two-state Markov availability model, fit a growth model to defect discovery times and compute how much failure-free testing is needed for a given confidence.

tasks.title: Build a two-state up and down Markov model with failure and repair rates and solve for steady-state probabilities
Fit the Goel-Okumoto model to weekly defect counts and predict the remaining defects and the release date at a target failure rate
Compute the failure-free test hours needed to claim a failure probability below one in 10,000 per demand at 99 percent confidence and discuss feasibility

schedule.title: Safety and security together
schedule.exercise: Analyse a pump hacking case with safety and security methods together, extend the STPA with attacker-caused unsafe control actions, and write an incident report.

tasks.title: Classify six attacks on medical devices and vehicles by the safety hazards they could trigger in an attack case file
Extend an STPA control structure with an attacker and list the additional unsafe control actions with a mitigation for each
Run a post-incident investigation of a ventilator fault, finding root causes and recommending actions that respect just culture, scored by rubric

schedule.title: Organisations, ethics and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present the safety case for the capstone system, including hazards, fault tree, redundancy design, reliability numbers and the residual risk statement.

tasks.title: Choose the key elements of a safety management system for a small hospital engineering team in a case and justify each against the rubric
Handle a liability case in which a software update caused harm, weighing duty of care, regulation and disclosure, scored by the rubric
Defend the capstone safety case before a simulated regulator, answering challenges on evidence, assumptions, residual risk and change control
